items.detail: The pullback from Thursday's record is now a pattern, not a pause — the **S&P 500 fell 53.30 points (-0.69%) to 7,691.76** on Tuesday, a **third straight loss**, with the Nasdaq sliding alongside it as semiconductors led the decline.
items.why: The bond market took over as the dominant equity driver, with a fresh 19-year high in the 30-year Treasury yield repricing long-duration growth stocks while oil kept climbing on the unresolved US-Iran standoff.

items.detail: The long end broke out: the **30-year Treasury yield topped 5.33%**, its **highest level since 2007** and a 19-year high, capping a global long-bond selloff.
items.why: Investors are pricing in surging government spending and a flood of long-dated supply on top of inflation that has now run above the Fed's target for five straight years, with the July federal deficit at $432.3 billion and the year-to-date shortfall near $1.8 trillion.

items.detail: Chips were the epicentre of the damage — **Wolfspeed sank 7.6%** into its August 19 earnings report on persistent negative-margin concerns, while optical-components maker **Fabrinet plunged 11.3%** despite beating on fiscal Q4 results.
items.why: Fabrinet's beat was overshadowed by weaker margins, negative free cash flow and a softer near-term profit outlook, and the surge in global bond yields amplified the de-rating across the whole semiconductor complex.

items.detail: The consumer's first real read since Friday's retail-sales collapse came in reassuring: **Home Depot's Q2 net sales rose 5.7% to $47.861 billion** versus $47.24 billion expected, **adjusted EPS was $4.92**, **same-store sales accelerated to +1.7%** from +1.0% a year ago, and full-year guidance was reaffirmed — sending the stock **up 1.01% to $341.30** against a falling tape.
items.why: The beat came from ticket rather than traffic — comparable average ticket rose 2.8% to $92.50 while comparable transactions fell 1.0% — so the strength reflects pricing and big-ticket pro demand holding up, not a broad rebound in household footfall.

items.detail: The calendar tightens from here: **July FOMC minutes land Wednesday** (from the 9-3 hold at 3.50-3.75%), **Target, Lowe's and TJX report Wednesday** and **Walmart Thursday**, before the **Jackson Hole symposium on August 27-29** delivers **Kevin Warsh's first keynote as Fed chair on Friday, August 28**.
items.sourceName: Federal Reserve Bank of Kansas City

items.detail: The post-holiday reopening has been one-way traffic — the **Nifty 50 fell 132.75 points (-0.55%) to 24,154.90** on Tuesday, its **sixth consecutive losing session**, while the **Sensex dropped 492.70 points (-0.63%) to 77,235.46** for a third straight decline.
items.why: Brent pushing above $91 a barrel on renewed US-Iran tensions combined with continued FII selling, the 19-year high in US long-bond yields and a weaker rupee to hit every leg of the Indian bull case at once.

items.detail: IT replaced energy as the source of the damage — **Nifty IT fell about 1.9%** and **Realty about 1.4%**, with **Tata Motors Passenger Vehicles (-2.24% to ₹322.80)**, **Asian Paints, Wipro, HCL Tech and Infosys all down more than 2%**; **Axis Bank led gainers at +1.28% to ₹1,243** and breadth was brutal at **11 advancers to 39 decliners**.
items.why: The spike in US long yields hits Indian IT twice over — as a valuation de-rating on long-duration earnings and as a signal of weaker discretionary tech spending by their US clients — while Tata Motors extended the succession-driven unwind rather than stabilising.

items.detail: The crude squeeze has a physical cause now, not just a rhetorical one — **only five commodity vessels transited the Strait of Hormuz on Saturday and none on Sunday**, against **31 the previous weekend**, after attacks on tankers, with **Brent near $90.97**.
items.why: Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araqchi said Tehran has not decided whether to resume talks with Washington, and renewed fighting in Lebanon plus the tanker attacks have made shipowners self-sanction the waterway regardless of whether a formal closure is ever declared.

items.detail: The currency is transmitting the oil shock directly — the **rupee weakened 7 paise to 95.68 per dollar** in early Tuesday trade, from **Monday's 95.61 close**, with Brent near $91.
items.why: Every dollar on crude widens India's import bill and lifts corporate demand for dollars, so the rupee is being sold as a proxy for the energy deficit rather than on any domestic data.

items.detail: Domestic money is still the only thing standing between this market and a much larger drawdown — on Monday **FIIs sold a net ₹2,535.10 crore** in the cash segment while **DIIs bought a net ₹5,101.50 crore**.
items.why: Domestic institutions are absorbing roughly twice the foreign selling with steady SIP inflows, which is why a six-session losing streak has cost the Nifty only around 1% rather than producing a capitulation.

items.detail: The break below $63,000 did not hold — **Bitcoin reclaimed $64,000**, opening Tuesday at **$64,487.65**, some **2.7% above Monday's open** and roughly **2.2% higher over 24 hours**, after bottoming near **$62,700**.
items.why: Spot bitcoin ETFs flipped back to daily inflows after four sessions of redemptions, restoring the marginal buyer whose absence had been the specific reason the $63,000 level failed on Friday.

items.detail: The four-day, $332 million ETF bleed reversed in a single session — **US spot bitcoin ETFs took in a net $297.5 million**, led by **BlackRock's IBIT at +$160.2 million**, **Fidelity's FBTC at +$111.9 million**, **ARK's ARKB at +$14.2 million** and **Morgan Stanley's MSBT at +$11.2 million**.
items.why: IBIT swung from being the single largest source of redemptions two sessions running to the largest buyer, meaning the outflow was a short repricing episode rather than a structural withdrawal of institutional allocation.

items.detail: Washington moved from statute to enforceable rule — the **Treasury issued a Notice of Proposed Rulemaking on August 17** implementing **Section 3 of the GENIUS Act**, published in the Federal Register Tuesday, opening a **60-day comment period closing October 19**; **stablecoin licensing becomes mandatory on January 18, 2027** and **US platforms may only offer stablecoins from licensed issuers from July 18, 2028**.
items.why: This is the first time the government has defined in formal rule language what it means to issue a US payment stablecoin and which businesses fall inside the law's perimeter, converting a 2025 statute into a compliance deadline issuers must now build against.

items.detail: Solana's headline upgrade did not actually land — the **August 17 Agave 4.2 activation target passed with the mainnet feature gates unconfirmed**, with Anza's tracker listing the **350ms and 300ms slot gates as pending with no activation epoch**, and the **90% rent cut and 4,096-byte transactions also lacking confirmed starts**.
items.why: Each change is gated independently and advances only on validator adoption, with the slot-time cut structured as four separate 50ms steps that each require the prior stage to run stably — so hitting the release date was never the same as shipping the features, and Alpenglow remains deferred to Agave 4.3 in October.

items.detail: Ether joined the bounce without escaping its range — **ETH rebounded 1.89% to about $1,909** on roughly **$18.4 million of spot ETF inflows**, with **BitMine adding 9,926 ETH to bring its holdings to 5,815,164 coins (about 4.8% of supply)**, while the **Crypto Fear & Greed Index sat at 30**, still in fear.
items.why: The move was driven by short covering and ETH-specific ETF and staking demand rather than any broad risk appetite, which is why sentiment readings stayed in fear territory even as prices rose.

crossCuttingTheme: Oil has handed the baton to the long bond: with Brent above $91 on the Hormuz shipping freeze keeping inflation sticky and the July deficit at $432.3 billion widening the year-to-date gap to $1.8 trillion, the 30-year Treasury yield's break to a 19-year 5.33% is now the single mechanism repricing all three markets — crushing long-duration US semiconductors into a third straight S&P 500 loss, dragging Indian IT down 1.9% while the same dollar strength pushed the rupee to 95.68, and leaving crypto as the lone decoupler, where a $297.5 million ETF inflow day let Bitcoin reclaim $64,000 in defiance of the rates backdrop.
